# QA report — feature-tie-capacity / U2 (REQ-TIECAP-1, REQ-TIECAP-11), attempt 1

Verdict: **PASS**. Unit under test: `agent/feature-tie-capacity/U2` @ `d9235f0` (draft PR #18, base `agent/rca-backfeed/fix`). QA model/mode: ultra (Coding ran on normal, STD-QA-1).

## 1. Prepare
- Standards confirmed from the brief: STD-GOV v1.1, STD-QA v1.3, STD-SAFETY v3.1.
- Read `.agents/skills/safety-critical-change/SKILL.md`, `DEMO_NOTES.md`, design `docs/specs/feature-tie-capacity/design.md` (§2, §6.1, §6.3 P1, §7, §11) on `agent/feature-tie-capacity/design`.
- Environment: Python 3.12.13, pydantic 2.14.1, fastapi 0.143.2 (design measured 0.143.1; same behaviour observed).

## 2. Execute — re-run of the repo commands (STD-QA-2)
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm --prefix console ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm --prefix console run build` | exit 0 — `dist/assets/index-DvMiGgeB.js 159.79 kB`, built in 446 ms |
| `ruff check backend` | `All checks passed!` |
| `pytest backend -q` on U2 head | `116 passed, 5 xfailed, 1 warning` |
| `pytest backend -q` with the QA oracle file added | `205 passed, 5 xfailed, 1 warning` |

## 3. Execute — independent oracle (STD-QA-3, STD-SAFETY-6)
File: `backend/tests/test_flisr_tie_capacity_qa_u2.py` on `agent/feature-tie-capacity/qa-U2` (89 tests, all pass).
- Oracle restates REQ-TIECAP-1 / Q-SPEC-9 / Q-SPEC-13 in closed form from spec literals: field set exactly `{kw, timestamp, quality}`; `kw` a JSON number (int or float, not bool/str/null); `timestamp` a string matching a strict ISO-8601 extended profile with a mandatory `Z` or `±HH:MM` offset, instant computed by the oracle itself; `quality` a string. No import of `app.flisr`/`app.network`; `app.models` imported for data types only (design §6.3, Q-DESIGN-1).
- Agreement measured on both validation paths — `TieCapacity.model_validate_json` (JSON mode) and a FastAPI `TestClient` route whose body is `{"tie_capacity": {"<mRID>": TieCapacity}}`, the exact nesting `POST /flisr/plan` will use (Python mode):
  - 49 named vectors (all brief vectors: `"yesterday"`, `1790000000`, naive `2026-10-15T22:00:00`, `"2000"`, `true`, extra field → reject; `NaN`, `-1.0`, `+02:00` → accept; plus `1790000000.0`, `"1790000000"`, naive with fraction, date-only, null, bool, empty string, `+24:00`, `24:00:00`, month 13, `"NaN"` string, false, arrays, objects, case-variant key, each missing field, empty object; accepts `±inf`, `0.0`, `-0.0`, integer literal, `1489.5`, `1489.4`, `-05:00`, `+00:00`, fractional seconds, no seconds, far past/future, any quality string). Agreement 49/49 on both paths; accepted values round-trip with the oracle's instant, kw (NaN-aware) and quality.
  - 600 seeded random bodies (`random.Random(20261016)`) over the kw / timestamp / quality / structure pools (≥ 100 accepted and ≥ 100 rejected asserted). Agreement 600/600 on both paths. Tolerance: exact (type and instant equality); no numeric tolerance applies to a type contract.
- Python-mode (direct caller) vectors: aware datetime (UTC and +02:00), ISO string, int kw, NaN kw → accept; naive datetime, `date`, int/float/bytes timestamp, str/bool kw, bytes quality, extra kwarg → reject.
- REQ-TIECAP-11: `TieBlockReason` values and names exactly `[FAULTED_SECTION, CAPACITY_INVALID, CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, CAPACITY_STALE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED]` in that order (Q-DESIGN-3 amendment), also in the OpenAPI enum; `BlockedTie` accepts each reason by value and rejects 9 malformed payloads; `RestorationPlan.blocked_ties` defaults to a fresh `[]`, a base-shaped JSON document still validates, the eight pre-existing fields and defaults equal the base @ 20d2a30, field order is base + `blocked_ties`, a three-entry list round-trips over HTTP in order, `blocked_ties` is optional in the response schema, and `None` / string / unknown reason / missing reason are rejected.
- Ad-hoc probes beyond the test file (recorded, no FAIL): `fromisoformat` also accepts the ISO-8601 variants `2026-10-15 22:00:00Z` (space separator), `+0200` (basic-format offset) and `2026-W42-4T22:00:00Z` (week date) and rejects lower-case `z`; a JSON body with duplicate `kw` keys is validated on the last value; in Python mode `kw=Decimal("1.0")` is accepted by `StrictFloat` (unreachable over HTTP). All are inside "ISO-8601 string"/"JSON number" and outside the spec's reject classes.

## 4. Execute — three failure modes (STD-QA-4)
- Model/logic mixing: `models.py` diff is declarative (constants, `Annotated` types, three models, one field). QA ast checks: no `if/for/while/try/match`, no clock call (`now/utcnow/today/time/...`), no `import time`, no import outside stdlib+pydantic. Independent of Coding's own ast test.
- Deleted error handling: the diff vs `agent/rca-backfeed/fix` removes only the two old import lines (re-grouped); no `try/except/raise` or validator removed; U1's two test files are untouched (`git diff origin/agent/feature-tie-capacity/U1..HEAD` lists only the four U2 files).
- Missing input treated as zero: `TieCapacity` has three required fields (`is_required()` asserted), `extra="forbid"`; the only new default is `blocked_ties = []` (a list, additive). No numeric default anywhere in the diff.

## 5. Execute — requirement coverage (STD-QA-6)
Collected with a pytest plugin reading the `requirement` marker on U2 head: REQ-TIECAP-1 → 72 passing tests (12 test functions in `test_flisr_tie_capacity_models.py`); REQ-TIECAP-11 → 10 passing + 1 strict xfail (`test_req_tiecap_11_held_tie_reported_as_faulted_section`, flipped by U3 per Q-CODE-U2-1 / design §6.1). The QA file adds 89 more (marked REQ-TIECAP-1 module-wide, REQ-TIECAP-11 on the eight blocked-ties tests).

## 6. Execute — repo contract and governance
- Q-CODE-U2-1 option (a): edits in `test_flisr_characterization.py` and `test_flisr_def_flisr_7.py` are limited to `model_dump(exclude={"blocked_ties"})` plus `assert plan.blocked_ties == []`, and one new strict-xfail test for FAULTED_SECTION; no expected step, order, customer count or `transferred_load_kw` changed (diff inspected line by line).
- Files touched by U2 are inside the amended unit file list (Q-CODE-1, Q-CODE-U2-1). `tools/`, `firmware/`, `legacy/` untouched.
- PR #18: open, draft, label `ai-generated`, head `d9235f0`, base `agent/rca-backfeed/fix` (Q-CODE-U1-2). All five U2 commits carry `AI-Governance: run=feature-tie-capacity stage=coding agent=devin model=normal`.
- CI on `d9235f0`: `backend` job red (pre-existing UP017 in `tools/build_coverage_report.py`, accepted under Q-CODE-U1-1), `native` and `ui` green.
- STD-GOV-7: the platform appends `Co-Authored-By: <git user name> <email>` to every commit (Coding's and QA's). Agents cannot change the git identity; reported for human action, as in prior stages.

## 7. Findings (none blocks PASS for U2)
- **F-QA-U2-1 (for U3, REQ-TIECAP-13).** FastAPI's default `RequestValidationError` handler echoes the rejected `input`. When a `TieCapacity` body is rejected for a *missing field* and its `kw` is JSON `NaN`/`Infinity`, the echo is not JSON-serialisable (`ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant`) and the response is **500**, not 422. Measured: `{"kw": NaN, "timestamp": "2026-10-15T22:00:00Z"}` → 500 on a plain `TieCapacity` route; `kw: Infinity` + extra field → 422 (the echo is the extra value only). models.py's verdict is correct (reject), so this is not a U2 defect; U3's endpoint must install a 422 handler that does not echo non-finite input (the QA harness does exactly that, see the comment in the test file). Today's `POST /flisr/plan` is not affected because `FlisrRequest` ignores extras and has no `TieCapacity` field.
- **Observation.** `BlockedTie` does not forbid extra fields (it is an output type; the spec does not require it). `IsoAwareDatetime` accepts every `datetime.fromisoformat` form, which is broader than the oracle's extended profile (see §3); all are ISO-8601.
- **Note.** The brief's unit JSON still lists a 4-member reason enum; `units.json` was amended to 5 members (design §11, Q-DESIGN-3). The 5-member enum is correct.

## 8. Tool classification (STD-SAFETY-7)
No tool-certification credit claimed. pytest/ruff/pydantic/FastAPI usage is as argued in design §8.1 (T1/T2 support tools; pydantic/FastAPI are pre-existing runtime software whose validation behaviour is measured, not assumed). Finding for the assessor only.
